decisions.english_term: U and T are primitive recursive and therefore total
decisions.sense: Kleene normal form uses an output function U and a computation relation T; totality refers to evaluation/decision procedures, not to conflating their types.
decisions.chosen_arabic: $U$ دالة و$T$ علاقة عوديتان بدائيتان؛ ومن ثم ينتهي حساب الأولى والبت في الثانية لكل مدخل.
decisions.grammatical_realization: Two explicitly different singular type nouns, joined by the feminine dual predicate عوديتان بدائيتان; الأولى refers to the function and الثانية to the relation.
decisions.rationale: The MSA noun الدالتان incorrectly explicitly types both objects as functions. T(e,x,s) occurs as a truth-valued witness condition under existential quantification, while U returns an output number. The Classical source already states the function/relation distinction. MSA now propagates that distinction and makes termination refer separately to function evaluation and deciding the relation. This preserves partiality of f: its unbounded witness search can fail to terminate even though each individual T test is decidable.
decisions.mathematical_argument: A ternary relation is a set of input triples/truth condition; its characteristic function is a different object encoding that truth condition. Total primitive-recursive U and decidable T do not imply a witness exists for every (e,x). Thus no claim that f is total is introduced.

alternatives.reason: Conflates T with its characteristic function without saying so.
Could suggest a total relation or universal truth; evaluation and decision termination are the intended properties.
Already distinguishes the object types in the preceding Classical clause; the present explanation for retaining it is retrospective, not a recovered original author rationale.

confidence.reason: Directly supported by the preserved predicate uses and output-function expression; terminology authority not consulted.

decisions.expert_review_reason: Check whether حساب الدالة / البت في العلاقة clearly separates evaluating a numerical output from deciding a predicate.

Recall that the Kleene normal form theorem states that every partial
computable function~$f$ has an index~$e$ such that $f(x) =
U(\umin{s}{T(e,x,s)})$ for all $x \in \Nat$, where $U$ and $T$ are
primitive recursive and therefore total. Thus, $f(x)$ is defined
(i.e., the computation halts) iff there is an~$s$ such that $T(e,x,s)$
holds.

decisions.english_term: whatever falls under the interpretation of P does not fall under the interpretation of R and vice versa
decisions.sense: A universally quantified biconditional P(z) iff not R(z) says the two predicate extensions are exact complements in the same domain, not merely disjoint.
decisions.chosen_arabic: MSA: ما يقع تحت تأويل P هو بالضبط ما لا يقع تحت تأويل R في المجال. Classical: ما يندرج تحت تأويل P هو بعينه ما لا يندرج تحت تأويل R في المجال.
decisions.grammatical_realization: The identity construction هو بالضبط / هو بعينه makes the two extensions exhaustive as well as disjoint; في المجال bounds negation to the structure's domain.
decisions.rationale: The English 'and vice versa' formulation can merely repeat mutual non-overlap, and both Arabic first-order glosses inherited that weakness. A biconditional requires every domain element to fall under exactly one of the predicates. Both registers are corrected here; this is a shared source-gloss correction, not just propagation from an already-correct Classical first-order sentence. The two Arabic phrasings preserve their registers without changing any formal expressions.
decisions.mathematical_argument: For any domain D and subsets A,B, all z in D satisfy (z in A iff z not in B) exactly when A=D\B, equivalently B=D\A. Necessity and sufficiency follow element by element; the relation requires disjointness AND A union B = D.
decisions.counterexample: D={1,2,3}, P-extension={1}, R-extension={2}. Both directional disjointness implications hold, but at 3 the biconditional has false left side and true right side. The weak gloss therefore omits exhaustiveness.

alternatives.reason: Permits a third domain element in neither extension.
A compact technical label alone requires an additional definition and may carry a different sense; the exact extension description is self-contained.
Both express equality of the predicate extension with the domain-relative complement.

confidence.reason: Elementwise biconditional equivalence and explicit three-element counterexample.

decisions.expert_review_reason: Check that the identity phrase conveys exact domain-relative complement rather than disjointness or implication.

decisions.english_term: there is still only a single value of the expression
decisions.sense: Confluence gives uniqueness of a normal form if one exists; it does not imply normalization or termination of every reduction strategy.
decisions.chosen_arabic: فلا تكون له نتيجتان نهائيتان مختلفتان؛ ولا تضمن هذه الخاصية وحدها وجود نتيجة نهائية.
decisions.grammatical_realization: Negate the existence of two distinct final results and separately deny that this property guarantees the existence of a final result.
decisions.rationale: The MSA introductory clause repeats the English's unqualified single-value phrasing. Both later proof paragraphs explicitly condition normal-form uniqueness on existence, and Classical's introduction does not assert existence. MSA now makes that same qualification explicit, without claiming every reduction path terminates whenever some normal form exists.
decisions.mathematical_argument: If a term reduces to two normal forms P and Q, confluence supplies a common reduct N. A normal form has no proper reduction, so both paths to N are trivial and P=Q. This proves at most one normal form, not at least one.
decisions.counterexample: Omega=(lambda x.x x)(lambda x.x x) has a single beta-redex and reduces back to itself. No normal form is reachable, although its reachable reduction component is confluent. A one-vertex self-loop is also a finite confluent rewrite-system counterexample to the general inference confluence=>normal-form existence.

alternatives.reason: May be read as asserting existence.
Correct but a trailing condition is easier to overlook; the selected two clauses explicitly distinguish uniqueness from existence.

alternatives.form: كل سبيل ينتهي إلى القيمة نفسها
alternatives.reason: Would additionally and falsely claim termination of every strategy.

confidence.reason: The existing conditional proof plus the explicit non-normalizing self-reduction separate the claims.

decisions.expert_review_reason: Check that نتيجتان نهائيتان مختلفتان is clear and that the second clause does not suggest the existence of normal forms is impossible.
decisions.expert_question: هل يبين النص أن الخاصية تمنع اختلاف نتيجتين نهائيتين إن وجدتا، ولا تضمن أن للحساب نتيجة نهائية أصلًا، من غير أن يوهم استحالة وجودها؟ الصياغة مفتوحة للتصحيح.
